title: Console UX: Region pinning settings + validation/errors + recent violations view
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Background
- We are introducing Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning + deterministic routing). Enterprise customers need a Console surface to (1) configure allowed/pinned regions, (2) understand enforcement behavior and warnings, (3) troubleshoot denial errors via recent violations + remediation tips.
- This ticket covers design + UX copy for Console settings UI and supporting surfaces (inline validation, empty states, violation summary module).

Primary users
1) Security/Compliance admin (enterprise): wants EU-only processing guarantee, needs evidence trail and clear guardrails.
2) Platform engineer (customer): wants to set correct config once, avoid surprises during deploys, and quickly debug new errors.
3) Support/CS internal user (secondary): needs a quick view of recent violations for triage.

Scope (what we are designing)
A) Settings page/module
- Location: Console → Org Settings (or Project Settings) → “Data residency” section.
- Configuration objects (expected from product/eng):
  - pinned_region: single selection (e.g., eu-west)
  - allowed_regions: multi-select (e.g., [eu-west, eu-central])
  - allow_cross_region_fallback: boolean (default off; may be hidden behind feature flag / exception process)
  - enforcement_mode: (implied) “Enforced” vs “Monitor-only” may exist during rollout; confirm with PM/eng.

B) Validation + warnings
- Validation errors are shown inline before save, plus server-side errors surfaced after save attempt.
- Clear warnings on capacity/failover semantics when pinned:
  - “No cross-region fallback: requests will be denied if capacity is unavailable in the pinned region.”
  - Link out to docs / exception request process.

C) Recent violations visibility
- A compact summary panel on the same page: counts over last 24h / 7d, latest 5 events, and a link to full Audit Logs filtered view (if available).
- Each violation row should show: timestamp, requested region/endpoint, evaluated region, decision, reason/error code, request_id, and “Recommended fix”.

Out of scope
- Full audit log explorer IA overhaul.
- Historical data migration / retention UI.
- Private/VPC on-prem UI beyond a clear “Not applicable / handled in your deployment” state (unless PM requests otherwise).

Key UX decisions to make (open questions)
1) Settings level: Org vs Project vs Workspace
- Product direction: policy can be set at org/project/workspace with precedence rules.
- Proposal for Console v1:
  - Show effective policy at current scope with a “Source of truth” indicator:
    - “Inherited from Org (Redwood EU-only)” or “Overridden at Project”.
  - Provide navigation to the scope that owns the setting.
  - Avoid silent overrides.
- Need confirmation from PM (Naomi Feldman / Marissa Cole) on which scope is editable in beta.

2) Region naming in UI
- Display friendly names + provider mapping:
  - “EU (Ireland) — eu-west”
  - “US (N. Virginia) — us-east”
- Keep the stable region code visible for SDK/base URL troubleshooting.

3) Allowed regions vs pinned region interaction
- Guardrails:
  - If pinned_region is set, it must be included in allowed_regions.
  - If allowed_regions has exactly one value, optionally auto-set pinned_region = that value (or prompt).
  - If allowed_regions has multiple values but pinned_region empty, show warning: “Requests may route to any allowed region; set a pinned region for deterministic residency.”

4) Rollout/flag handling in UI
- During beta, some orgs may see “Monitor-only” or partial enforcement.
- UI must reflect actual state to reduce confusion:
  - Badge: “Enforced” / “Monitor-only (beta)” / “Not enabled for your plan”.
  - If not enabled: show read-only explanation and CTA to contact Sales/Support.

Information architecture proposal
- Section header: Data residency
- Tabs or subsections:
  1) Residency policy
     - Allowed regions (multi-select)
     - Pinned region (single-select; optional but recommended)
     - Cross-region fallback (toggle; default off; gated behind exception/feature flag)
     - Save / Cancel
  2) Recent residency decisions (summary)
     - Violations chart + latest events table + link to Audit Logs

Component/copy requirements
- Inline helper text (examples):
  - Allowed regions helper: “Requests and stored artifacts (prompts, completions, embeddings payloads, request metadata, logs, and optional persistence features) will be restricted to these regions.”
  - Pinned region helper: “When set, Redwood will only execute requests in this region. Cross-region fallback is disabled unless explicitly allowed.”

Warnings
- If pinned region set and fallback disabled:
  - Warning callout: “Strict enforcement enabled. If the pinned region is unavailable or at capacity, requests will be denied (HTTP 409/403 depending on error code mapping) rather than failing over to another region.”
- If user attempts to enable cross-region fallback (if visible):
  - Modal confirmation: “This may allow processing outside your pinned region during capacity events. Requires approval and will be audited.”
  - Secondary text: “Your organization’s exception policy and expiry will be recorded.”

Validation errors (client-side)
- “Select at least one allowed region.”
- “Pinned region must be one of the allowed regions.”
- “Pinned region cannot be empty when ‘Deterministic routing’ is enabled.” (if we expose such a toggle)
- “You don’t have permission to edit data residency settings.” (RBAC)

Save-time / server errors (examples)
- Policy conflict (server): “Policy could not be saved because it conflicts with an inherited org-level restriction.”
- Feature not available (plan): “Data residency controls are available on Enterprise plans. Contact Sales to enable.”
- Temporary backend failure: “Couldn’t save settings. Try again, or contact Support if this persists.”

Recent violations module
- Summary metrics:
  - “Violations (last 24h)” + “Violations (last 7d)”
  - Optional: “Denied requests (last 24h)” to separate decision types
- Latest events table columns:
  - Time
  - Error code (e.g., RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH)
  - Requested region/endpoint (if available)
  - Evaluated region
  - Reason snippet
  - Request ID (copy)
  - Action: “View in Audit Logs” (deep link with filters)
- Empty states:
  - No data: “No residency violations detected in the last 7 days.”
  - Not enabled: “Enable enforcement to start collecting residency decisions.” (if applicable)

Accessibility / usability notes
- Multi-select regions must be keyboard navigable.
- Keep warnings as non-blocking unless they imply invalid state.
- Provide “Copy policy as JSON” (optional nice-to-have) for sharing with Support; confirm with eng if feasible.

Deliverables
- Figma frames covering:
  1) Default state (not enabled / read-only)
  2) Enabled with allowed_regions only
  3) Enabled with pinned_region + strict enforcement warning
  4) Validation error states
  5) Save confirmation toast + audit event hint (“Changes will appear in Audit Logs within ~1 minute”)
  6) Recent violations: populated + empty
- Copy deck (strings) for warnings and validation messages.
- Handoff notes for ENG-2846 implementation (API fields and expected behaviors).

Acceptance criteria (design)
- Clear mental model of “Allowed regions” vs “Pinned region” with guardrails.
- Explicit and prominent warning about strict enforcement behavior (denies vs fallback).
- Users can understand why requests are being denied and how to fix (endpoint/SDK region mismatch) from the same page.
- Design includes plan gating + RBAC read-only experience.

Links / references
- PRD: PRD hosted data residency enforcement (Confluence)
- Design spec: Region pinning and enforcement (Confluence)
- Error codes: Data residency error codes (Confluence)
- Audit event spec: Audit events data residency (Confluence)

Owners / reviewers (to confirm)
- PM: Naomi Feldman (security & compliance)
- Eng (Console): Chloe Martin / Dylan Brooks
- Security: Marcus Lin (copy review for compliance semantics)
- Support readiness: Dev Patel (ensure troubleshooting guidance matches playbooks)

Open questions for PM/Eng (please answer in comments)
1) For beta: is the editable scope org-only, project-only, or both?
2) Do we expose “allow_cross_region_fallback” in UI at all, or only via exception workflow/internal tooling?
3) What’s the expected deep link target for “View in Audit Logs”? Do we already have an audit log UI with filters?
4) Are we showing decision events (allow/deny) or only violations in the Console summary?
5) What exact HTTP code(s) and error payload fields should be referenced in troubleshooting copy (so it matches API standards)?
comments: 2025-01-24 — Marissa Cole: Please optimize for enterprise admins first. Most urgent is preventing confusion when pinned EU orgs hit US base URL and start seeing denials. The settings page should make the correct endpoint obvious.
2025-01-28 — Felix Schneider: For “Recent violations”, we can likely query audit events once ENG-2844 lands. We should design it so it degrades gracefully (empty state) if audit pipeline is delayed.

2025-02-03 — Chloe Martin: Confirming Console backend will expose: allowed_regions[], pinned_region, effective_policy_scope, and a violations_summary endpoint (counts + latest events). Please include states for inherited policy + no edit permission.
